doc.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Thanks, plans for the Hamilton archive, and Dance's donated collection
summary: Rowe describes the archive opening near Syracuse; Dance mentions sending magazines and LPs to Yale.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well this has been a fascinating hour for me. And on behalf of jazz lovers everywhere, I’d like to thank you for your output over the years.
Your involvement in the music — it’s been great to have someone who’s been able to gather all the stories of these musicians.
Well just tell me, before I hand it over to Helen, just tell me what is the archive planning to do then, beside these interviews?
We will, as we plan our guidelines, we’re officially opening in October.
But we’re not open yet. But it will be a place, somewhat like Rutgers, where you can visit, and researchers and students and authors can view the interviews, read the transcripts—
We’re in Central New York. We’re right near Syracuse, outside Syracuse.
Oh, I see, up there, yeah.

And I would like to set up a program where other music schools could borrow our tapes much like a library. Now we’re treading a line here with keeping the musicians so that they don’t feel like they’re being taken advantage of you know. But we’ve amassed a nice collection of things, and it’s been a real honor for me to actually meet so many musicians.
Well are you sort of thinking of accumulating stuff like Rutgers?

Yes. We hope to start a collection of LP’s and photographs from, especially the musicians we’ve talked to, and we’ve made a small start on that. And in support of the interviews it would be nice to have material like that.

Yeah. I sent a large part of my — I sent photographs, magazines, and LPs to Yale. And that was partly to raise some scratch. But also, you know, the house is reasonable so I spent — it’s amazing how it accumulates you know, the books and stuff. But the magazines are a problem, aren’t they.
Yeah, they are. They take up a lot of space and you know they deteriorate.
Yeah well I had Down Beat I remember complete, and that went to Yale, and Metronome I had the best years of. But that’s something you’ll have to face eventually.
